title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #999: The Duffin-Schaeffer Conjecture**

For any f: ℕ → ℕ, these are equivalent:
1. Almost all α have infinitely many coprime (p,q) with |α - p/q| < f(q)/q
2. ∑ φ(q)·f(q)/q = ∞

**Status:** SOLVED (Koukoulopoulos-Maynard, 2020)

This was one of the most famous open problems in metric number theory, open for 79 years (1941-2020). It generalizes Khintchine's theorem to non-monotone approximation functions.
mathContext: The conjecture connects two seemingly different conditions: a measure-theoretic statement about 'almost all' reals and an arithmetic series involving Euler's totient. The φ(q) factor accounts for the coprimality requirement.

title: Core Definitions
content:
**eulerPhi n:** Wrapper for Nat.totient — counts integers ≤ n coprime to n. Appears in the Duffin-Schaeffer sum because φ(q)/q measures the density of reduced fractions with denominator q.

**IsApproximable α f q:** There exists coprime p with |α - p/q| < f(q)/q. The coprimality condition (p,q)=1 is essential — without it, the equivalence fails.

**IsInfinitelyApproximable α f:** Approximable for infinitely many q. Formalized as ∀ N, ∃ q > N with IsApproximable α f q.
mathContext: The coprimality constraint distinguishes this from Khintchine's setup. Without it, the same rational p/q appears with every multiple denominator, inflating the count.

title: Duffin-Schaeffer Sum and Divergence
content:
**DuffinSchaefferSum f N:** The partial sum ∑_{q=0}^{N} φ(q) · f(q) / q.

**SeriesDiverges f:** The sum grows without bound — ∀ M, ∃ N with DuffinSchaefferSum f N > M.

**SeriesConverges f:** The sum is bounded — ∃ L, ∀ N, DuffinSchaefferSum f N ≤ L.

Divergence vs. convergence of this series completely determines the approximation behavior.
mathContext: The Duffin-Schaeffer sum is the natural analogue of the Khintchine series ∑ f(q)/q, corrected by the factor φ(q)/q to account for coprimality. For monotone f, both series have the same convergence behavior.

title: Measure-Theoretic Formulation
content:
**AlmostAll P:** Property P holds on a co-null subset of [0,1] — there exists S with P on S and volume(Icc 0 1 \ S) = 0.

**AlmostAllApproximable f:** Almost all α are infinitely f-approximable.

**AlmostNoneApproximable f:** Almost no α is infinitely f-approximable.

The conjecture says: SeriesDiverges f ↔ AlmostAllApproximable f.
mathContext: Using Lebesgue measure on [0,1] is standard in metric number theory. The 'almost all' quantifier means the exceptional set has measure zero.

title: The Duffin-Schaeffer Conjecture and Both Directions
content:
**DuffinSchaefferConjecture:** ∀ f, SeriesDiverges f ↔ AlmostAllApproximable f.

**easy_direction:** AlmostAllApproximable f → SeriesDiverges f. Follows from the Borel-Cantelli lemma — if the sum converges, the limsup set has measure zero.

**hard_direction:** SeriesDiverges f → AlmostAllApproximable f. This is the actual conjecture, open for 79 years. The difficulty is that approximation sets for different q can overlap in complex ways, preventing direct Borel-Cantelli application.
mathContext: The easy direction is a standard measure theory argument. The hard direction required Koukoulopoulos and Maynard to develop new graph-theoretic techniques on the 'GCD graph' to handle the overlaps.

title: Erdős's Partial Result and Koukoulopoulos-Maynard
content:
**ErdosCondition f:** ∃ C, ∀ q, f(q) · q ≤ C — the approximation function decays at least as fast as 1/q.

**erdos_bounded_case:** The conjecture holds when f·q is bounded. Erdős proved this special case.

**koukoulopoulos_maynard_2020:** The full DuffinSchaefferConjecture. Published in Annals of Mathematics 192(1), 251-307.

**duffin_schaeffer_theorem:** Named version, defined as koukoulopoulos_maynard_2020.
mathContext: Erdős's partial result handles the 'bounded' case where approximation intervals are uniformly small. The full conjecture allows f to be arbitrary, making overlap analysis much harder. Koukoulopoulos-Maynard's proof introduced the 'compression' technique on GCD graphs.

title: Consequences and Related Results
content:
**convergence_case:** If the series converges, almost no α is infinitely approximable.

**zero_one_law:** For any f, either almost all or almost none are approximable — no intermediate case. This follows from the Duffin-Schaeffer theorem: divergence gives 'all', convergence gives 'none'.

**continued_fraction_case:** f(q) = 1 gives almost all approximable. This is the classical continued fraction result.

**khintchine_theorem:** For monotone decreasing f, ∑ f(q)/q = ∞ ↔ almost all approximable. The 1924 precursor that Duffin-Schaeffer generalizes.

**LimsupSet f:** The set { α | IsInfinitelyApproximable α f } — the 'limsup' of approximation events.
mathContext: The zero-one law is a striking dichotomy: there is no function f for which exactly half of all reals are infinitely approximable. Khintchine's theorem requires monotonicity, which Duffin-Schaeffer removes at the cost of replacing ∑ f(q)/q with ∑ φ(q)·f(q)/q.
